locations.name: Red Soil
locations.summary: Odisha's most widely distributed soil — coarse, porous, iron-rich and acidic. Dominates the southern and south-western hill belt.

details.coverage: ≈ 7.14 million hectares (largest soil group — ~45% of Odisha)
details.formation: Decomposition of silicate and iron deposits of the upper Dharwar series under heavy rainfall.
details.texture: Coarse-textured, highly porous; strongly to moderately acidic.
details.fertility: Rich in iron, potassium and phosphorus; deficient in nitrogen and organic matter.

locations.name: Red and Yellow Soil
locations.summary: Second-largest soil group. Covers the northern plateau belt — coarse and acidic in uplands, finer and richer in lowlands.

details.formation: Weathering of ancient Precambrian rocks (gneisses, granites) under tropical climate.
details.texture: Upland: coarse, acidic. Lowland (alluvial deposits): finer, richer in potassium.
details.fertility: Lowland variants more productive due to alluvial enrichment.
details.notes: Dominant across the northern plateau belt of Odisha; upland vs. lowland variants behave quite differently.

locations.name: Laterite Soil
locations.summary: Deep red, iron-oxide-rich soil formed by intense leaching under tropical monsoon. Strongly acidic and low in fertility. Dominant in Mayurbhanj.

details.formation: Intense leaching of basaltic rocks and gneisses under tropical monsoon — iron and aluminium oxides accumulate as softer minerals wash away.
details.texture: Deep red to reddish-brown; high iron oxide content; strongly acidic.

locations.name: Alluvial Soil
locations.summary: Most fertile soil of Odisha — silt and clay deposited by the Mahanadi, Brahmani, Baitarani and Subarnarekha deltas. Excellent moisture retention.

details.formation: Silt and clay deposits laid down by east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Brahmani, Baitarani, Subarnarekha).
details.texture: Varies from sandy loam (north Baleswar) to heavy clay (Mahanadi delta). Slightly acidic to neutral.
details.fertility: Highly fertile; excellent moisture retention; best agricultural soil in Odisha.

locations.name: Black Soil
locations.summary: Heavy clay soil that swells when wet and cracks deeply in summer. Found in pockets of western Odisha. Neutral to alkaline, calcium-rich.

details.formation: Formed from basaltic parent rock in low-lying areas with poor drainage.
details.texture: Heavy; >30% clay; swells when wet, cracks deeply in summer; neutral to alkaline.
details.fertility: Rich in calcium; deficient in phosphorus and zinc.

locations.name: Mixed Red and Black Soil
locations.summary: Catenary mix — red soil on upper slopes, black soil in lower depressions. Medium fertility, neutral pH.

details.formation: Catenary formation: red soil on upper slopes merges into black soil in valley bottoms.
details.texture: Catenary: red soil upper, black soil lower; neutral pH.

locations.name: Saline Soil
locations.summary: Narrow tidal-affected coastal strip (5–25 km wide) around Chilika lake and the Puri–Kendrapara coastline. Highly alkaline due to salt-water incursion.

details.coverage: Narrow strip 5–25 km wide along the coast
details.formation: Tidal incursion and sea-water flooding deposits salts, raising soil alkalinity.
details.fertility: Poorly fertile due to salinity; needs reclamation.
details.notes: Concentrated around Chilika Lake and the Puri coast. Cultivation requires salt-tolerant varieties and drainage management.

locations.name: Brown Forest Soil
locations.summary: Light, acidic, organic-rich soil of the forested Eastern Ghats hill belt. Found mainly in Kandhamal and Ganjam. Threatened by Podu (shifting cultivation).

details.formation: Developed under dense forest cover in the Eastern Ghats; high organic content from leaf litter.
details.fertility: Rich in organic matter and nitrogen; low in phosphorus.
details.notes: Frequently subjected to Podu (shifting cultivation) by tribal communities, which causes soil degradation and topsoil loss.
